title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Geotechni. BÜW VE7531f NeM17 2. Stammstrecke München
description: Das Vorhaben der Netzergänzenden Maßnahme 17 (NeM17) ist durch den Infrastrukturbedarf auf den Außenästen des bestehenden S-Bahn-Netzes bedingt, der sich durch das ab Inbetriebnahme der 2. S-Bahn-Stammstrecke zugrunde zu legende Betriebsprogramm ergibt. Mit der 2. S-Bahn-Stammstrecke wird die Neuerrichtung einer zweigleisigen S-Bahn-Strecke, beginnend im Personenbahnhof München-Laim und endend im Bahnhofsteil München-Leuchtenbergring mit den dazwischenliegenden Haltepunkten Hauptbahnhof Bahnhofplatz, Marienhof und Ostbahnhof als Gesamtprojekt verfolgt. Zur Gewährleistung der Durchführbarkeit des Betriebsprogramms wird ein zweites Streckengleis auf der Ostseite des vorhandenen Gleises zwischen dem Hp Steinebach und dem Bf Seefeld-Hechendorf gebaut. Die Gleisanlagen, Ingenieurbauwerke, sowie die technische Ausrüstung werden für die Zweigleisigkeit angepasst bzw. erweitert. Ebenfalls umfasst der Projektumgriff die barrierefreie Erschließung der Verkehrsstation Steinebach. Weiterhin sind zwischen den Bf Weßling und Bf Herrsching Schallschutzmaßnahmen berücksichtigt. Das Vorhaben wird im Bereich der Strecke 5541 km 18,800 – 30,890 umgesetzt. Es befindet sich in den Gemeinden Weßling, Seefeld, Wörthsee und Herrsching a. Ammersee im Landkreis Starnberg, Bayern.

title: Finland – Translation services – Valtioneuvoston ja oikeuskanslerinviraston monikielisiä käännöspalveluita koskeva puitejärjestely 2027-2029 (2030/2031)
description: Valtioneuvoston kanslia (VNK) vastaa valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden yhteisistä hallinto- ja palvelutehtävistä. Valtioneuvoston kanslia huolehtii kaikkien ministeriöiden käännös- ja kielipalveluista sekä kansalliskielille että muille kielille. Lisäksi VNK huolehtii osin oikeuskanslerinviraston tarvitsemista käännös- ja kielipalveluista. Hankinnan kohteena on valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden monikielisiä käännöspalveluita koskevat puitejärjestelyt, jotka täydentävät valtioneuvoston ruotsin ja englannin kielten käännöspalveluita koskevia puitejärjestelyjä (VN/33137/2023). Lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat oikeuskanslerinviraston tarvitsemat käännöspalvelut (pois lukien oikeuskanslerinviraston ruotsin käännöspalvelut). Käännökset voivat koskea mitä tahansa ministeriöiden toimialoihin kuuluvaa asiaa, ks. valtioneuvoston ohjesääntö 262/2003, § 10–24, http://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2003/20030262. Lisätietoa ministeriöiden toimialoista on saatavilla myös ministeriöiden www-sivustoilla, ks. https://valtioneuvosto.fi/ministeriot. Oikeuskansleri valvoo hallituksen ja ministeriöiden sekä tasavallan presidentin virkatoimien lainmukaisuutta. Hän valvoo myös, että tuomioistuimet, viranomaiset ja virkamiehet sekä muut julkista tehtävää hoitavat noudattavat lakia ja täyttävät velvollisuutensa. Lisäksi oikeuskanslerilla on asianajajien valvontaan liittyviä tehtäviä. Oikeuskansleri toimii valtioneuvoston yhteydessä. Lisätietoa oikeuskanslerin tehtävistä ja oikeuskanslerinvirastosta: https://www.okv.fi/fi/. Oikeuskanslerinviraston käännöstarpeet koskevat osa-aluetta 2 ja erityisesti englannin käännöksiä. Satunnaisesti on tarvetta myös muiden kielten käännöksille pois lukien ruotsinkieliset käännökset. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen osa-alueeseen: Osa-alue 1 KKV- ja TES-käännökset (suomi-ruotsi) • ministereiden vastauksia kansanedustajien tekemiin kirjallisiin kysymyksiin (KKV) • työehtosopimuksia (TES) • valitaan kaksi (2) toimittajaa Osa-alue 2 Muut käännökset, useita kielipareja • raportteja ja selvityksiä ja niiden tiivistelmiä • verkkosivutekstejä • PowerPoint-esityksiä • valitaan kolme (3) toimittajaa Hankittavan palvelun kuvaus on esitetty tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus. Tarjoaja voi tarjota joko yhteen tai molempiin osa-alueisiin. Hankinnan perusteella perustetaan molemmille osa-alueille useamman toimittajan puitejärjestelyt. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on molemmat osa-alueet yhteenlaskettuna noin 475 000 euroa vuodessa ja valittavien toimittajien kanssa tehdään kahden vuoden määräaikaiset puitesopimukset, joissa varataan mahdollisuus käyttää kaksi optiovuotta (1+1). Sopimuskausi alkaa arviolta 1.2.2027.

title: Finland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Development of the Visit Northern Finland B2B-platform (competitive procedure with negotiation)
description: Visit Northern Finland Oy (hereinafter referred to as VNF or VNF Oy) is inviting tenders for the design, implementation and launch of a new business-to-business (B2B) online platform. This call for tenders is published on Hilma (hankintailmoitukset.fi) as a national procurement in accordance with the Act on Public Procurement and Concession Contracts (1397/2016). A user interface prototype already exists, which defines what the platform might look like and how it might function. This call for tenders concerns the implementation of the production platform to be built on this basis, including the integrations and features described in Chapter 4. This call for tenders includes annexes. Together with the prototype, these form part of the tender documentation. In the event of any discrepancies between the documents, the tenderer must raise the matter during the question-and-answer period; the call for tenders takes precedence. The procurement is being carried out as part of the Smart Growth for International Tourism (SmartGIT) project, co-funded by the European Union (https://visitoulu.fi/en/smart-growth-for-international-tourism-smartgit/).

title: France – Building completion work – Accords-cadres de travaux tous corps d’état (TCE) relatifs à la réalisation de petits travaux de bâtiments tertiaires, pour les besoins de la DI d’ENEDIS sur l’ensemble de la métropole.
description: Les présents accords-cadres portent sur des travaux de construction, d’aménagement, de restructuration, de désamiantage/démolition et d’entretien de bâtiments tertiaires, sur le territoire de la Direction Immobilière (DI) d’ENEDIS Accord cadre sans engagement financier Montant total de cet accord cadre 500 M € (Montant détaillé lot par lot) / 8 ans (3 ans fermes et 5 x 1an en option) Les accords-cadres sont principalement destinés à la réalisation de petites opérations de travaux de faible montant (dits « petits travaux immobiliers »), réalisés sur des sites multiples. Cet avis comprend 19 lots géographiques couvrant la métropole. - Pour l’ensemble de la consultation, le candidat pourra se positionner sur tout ou partie des lots 1 à 19. Le candidat peut se positionner sur la totalité des lots. Les lots géographiques se répartissent comme suit : La région NORD-EST d’Enedis : - Lot 1 : LILLE / AMIENS - Lot 2 : CAEN - Lot 3 : REIMS - Lot 4 : DIJON - Lot 5 : NANCY La région GRAND-OUEST d’Enedis : - Lot 6 : RENNES / QUIMPER - Lot 7 : NANTES - Lot 8 : POITIERS - Lot 9 : LIMOGES - Lot 10 : BOURGES - Lot 11 : BORDEAUX - Lot 12 : PAU La région SUD-EST d’Enedis : - Lot 13 : CLERMONT - Lot 14 : LYON - Lot 15 : CHAMBERY - Lot 16 : TOULOUSE - Lot 17 : MONTPELLIER - Lot 18 : AIX / MARSEILLE / NICE - Lot 19 : ILE DE FRANCE Les candidats doivent être en capacité de traiter les lots techniques suivants : • Démolition/ Gros Œuvre. • Revêtements Sols durs. • Métallerie Bardage. • Menuiseries Extérieur - Porte entrée. • Occultation Intérieur. • Occultation Extérieure. • Menuiserie Intérieur. • Faux Plancher. • Plâtrerie Fx Plafonds. • Cloisons amovibles. • Peint. Revêt muraux. • Revêtement sols souples. • CFA. • CFO. • CVC. • Plomberie. • Toitures terrasse étanchéité. • Désamiantage. A titre indicatif, la répartition prévisionnelle des opérations d’ENEDIS est la suivante : - 75% des opérations sont d’un montant inférieur à 100 000€, avec 60% inférieures à 50 000€. - 20% des opérations sont comprises entre 100 000 à 400 000€, avec un montant moyen de 250 000€ - Les 5% d’opérations restantes peuvent ponctuellement dépasser 400 000€. Ces opérations demeurent exceptionnelles et ne pourront excéder 1 000 000€. Le montant d’intervention peut être de 0 à 1 000 000 € Le présent accord-cadre sera exécuté selon les modalités suivantes : sans remise en concurrence des titulaires, pour : - pour les opérations dont le montant estimatif est inférieur ou égal à 100 000 €HT pour les lots 1 à 18 inclus - pour les opérations dont le montant estimatif est inférieur ou égal à 250 000 €HT pour le lot 19 IDF avec remise en concurrence des titulaires par marchés subséquents, pour : - les opérations dont le montant estimatif est supérieur au seuil de 100 000 € HT pour les lots 1 à 18 inclus. - les opérations dont le montant estimatif est supérieur au seuil de 250 000 € HT pour le lot 19 IDF Pour le lot 19, les titulaires du contrat seront consultés à tour de rôle.

title: 26127 Tulkkaus- ja käännöspalvelut
description: Seinäjoen kaupungin hankintapalvelut pyytää sitovaa tarjoustanne tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluista tämän tarjouspyynnön ehtojen mukaisesti. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä. Sopimuskausi alkaa kun sopimus on allekirjoitettu ja päättyy 31.12.2027. Tilaaja varaa itselleen oikeuden halutessaan jatkaa sopimusta yhdellä (1) vuodella (optio), 31.12.2028 saakka. Hankinnan kohteena ovat Seinäjoen kaupungin tarvitsemat tulkkaus- ja käännöspalvelut suomen kielestä vieraaseen kieleen ja vieraasta kielestä suomen kieleen. Tulkkauspalvelut toteutetaan pääosin ennalta varattavina etätulkkauksina. Läsnäolotulkkauksen tarve on marginaalinen. Palveluja käytetään kaupungin kotoutumispalveluissa, työllisyyspalveluissa, varhaiskasvatuksessa ja oppilaitoksissa. Seinäjoen kaupunki käyttää palveluita tarpeen mukaan, eikä sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana. Hankintaan sisältyy neljä palvelutuotetta: 1. Etätulkkaus (osa 1) 2. Pikatulkkaus (osa 2) 3. Läsnäolotulkkaus (osa 3) 4. Käännöspalvelut (osa 4) Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo noin 85 000 euroa vuodessa sekä optiomahdollisuus, ylittävät julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetun lain (hankintalaki 1397/2016) 25 §:n mukaisen kansallisen kynnysarvon, joten tarjouskilpailussa sovelletaan hankintalakia. Lisäksi hankinnassa noudatetaan tarjouspyynnön Muuta asiat -kohdassa ja liitteenä olevassa sopimusmallissa ilmoitettuja säädöksiä ja ohjeita., Ennalta varattava etätulkkaus Etätulkkauksella tarkoitetaan puhelin- tai videoyhteyden välityksellä toteutettavaa tulkkauspalvelua, jossa tulkki osallistuu tulkkaustapahtumaan etäyhteyden kautta eikä ole fyysisesti läsnä tulkkauspaikalla. Tarjoajalta edellytetään mahdollisuutta sekä puhelintulkkaukseen että tietoturvallisen videoyhteyden käyttöön tulkkaustapahtumassa. Suositus on, että käytössä on Teams-yhteys. Palvelua käytetään pääsääntöisesti arkipäivisin klo 8.00 - 17.00 ja tulkki tilataan ennakkoon. Tulkkauspalvelut tilataan palveluntuottajan sähköisen tilausjärjestelmän kautta ja tarvittaessa puhelimitse. Hankinnan kohteen kriteereissä on lueteltu vähimmäisvaatimukset tilausjärjestelmälle ja tulkkaustilanteissa käytettävien sovellusten teknisille ja toiminnallisille vaatimuksille. Palvelua arvioidaan tarvittavan 1440 tuntia vuoden aikana. Ennalta varattavan etätulkkauksen kielet on jaettu kahteen kieliryhmään sen perusteella, mihin kieliin tulkkaustarpeet eniten kohdistuvat. Jaottelu on arvio, joka todennäköisesti elää ja muuttuu sopimuskauden aikana. Kieliryhmien kielet on lueteltu hankinnan kohteen kriteereissä ja palvelukuvauksessa. Tarjouspyynnön vähimmäisvaatimuksina on, että palveluntuottajan tulee tässä osassa tarjota molempiin kieliryhmiin. Tilaaja vastaa tulkkauksen puhelinkuluista. Palvelu on kuvattu yksityiskohtaisemmin palvelukuvaus -liitteessä., Pikatulkkaus Pikatulkkaus kiireellisiin tulkkaustilanteisiin, jolloin tulkki tilataan ilman ennakkovarausaikaa. Pikatulkkaus toteutetaan etätulkkauksena pääsääntöisesti puhelinyhteydellä, mutta palveluntuottajan tulee varautua myös videoyhteyteen. Palvelua käytetään pääsääntöisesti arkipäivisin klo 8.00 - 17.00. Tulkkauspalvelut tilataan palveluntuottajan sähköisen tilausjärjestelmän kautta ja tarvittaessa puhelimitse. Hankinnan kohteen kriteereissä on lueteltu vähimmäisvaatimukset tilausjärjestelmälle ja tulkkaustilanteissa käytettävien sovellusten teknisille ja toiminnallisille vaatimuksille. Palvelua arvioidaan tarvittavan 160 tuntia vuoden aikana. Pikatulkkauksessa kielet on jaettu kahteen kieliryhmään sen perusteella, mihin kieliin tulkkaustarpeet eniten kohdistuvat. Jaottelu on arvio, joka todennäköisesti elää ja muuttuu sopimuskauden aikana. Kieliryhmien kielet on lueteltu hankinnan kohteen kriteereissä ja liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa. Tarjouspyynnön vähimmäisvaatimuksina on, että palveluntuottajan tulee tässä osassa tarjota molempiin kieliryhmiin. Tilaaja vastaa tulkkauksen puhelinkuluista. Palvelu on kuvattu yksityiskohtaisemmin palvelukuvaus -liitteessä Tilaaja vastaa tulkkauksen puhelinkuluista., Läsnäolotulkkaus Läsnäolotulkkaus on paikan päällä toteutettava tulkkauspalvelu, jossa tulkki saapuu tilaajan ilmoittamaan paikkaan ja suorittaa tulkkauksen fyysisesti läsnä olevana. Tulkkausta ei toteuteta puhelin- tai videoyhteyden välityksellä. Palvelua käytetään pääsääntöisesti arkipäivisin klo 8.00 - 17.00. Tulkkauspalvelut tilataan palveluntuottajan sähköisen tilausjärjestelmän kautta ja tarvittaessa puhelimitse. Läsnäolotulkkaukset pyritään tilaamaan vähintään 1 viikko ennen palvelun tarvetta. Palveluntuottajan on varauduttava myös kiireellisiin tilauksiin. Ensisijaisesti käytetään Seinäjoella tai mahdollisimman lähellä Seinäjokea asuvia tulkkeja. Tarjouspyynnön vähimmäisvaatimuksina on, että palveluntuottajan tulee tässä osassa tarjota kieliryhmän 1 kieliin, jotka on lueteltu hankinnan kohteen kriteereissä sekä palvelukuvauksessa. Palvelu on kuvattu yksityiskohtaisemmin palvelukuvaus -liitteessä Tarve läsnäolotulkkaukselle on vähäinen, arviolta 5 tuntia vuodessa. Tilaaja vastaa tulkin matkakuluista, joista sovitaan tilauksen yhteydessä., Käännöspalvelut Käännöstyössä palveluntuottaja noudattaa SKTL:n asiatekstikääntäjien hyvää käännöstapaa ja alkuperäisen tekstin ulkoasua. Käännökset ovat virheetöntä hyvää kieltä, jossa säilytetään lähdekielen asiasisältö ja tyyli muuttumattomina siten, että ne ovat käytettävissä virallisesti alkuperäisten asiakirjojen tavoin. Tavanomaisia käännöspalvelujen tarpeita ovat mm. asiakkaiden todistusten, viranomaispäätösten ja lääkärilausuntojen käännökset lähdekielestä suomen kielelle ja toisin päin. Aineistojen siirrossa käytetään suojattua sähköpostiyhteyttä. Käännöstyön toimitusaika arvioidaan tilauksen yhteydessä ja vahvistetaan tilausvahvistuksessa. Palveluntuottajalla tulee olla käytettävissä auktorisoituja kielenkääntäjiä vähintään seuraaviin kielipareihin: *suomi-englanti *suomi-arabia *suomi-venäjä Muut kielet, joihin on saatavilla auktorisoituja kääntäjiä, on ilmoitettava tarjouksessa. Hankinnan arvioitu määrä on noin 100 sivua/12 kk:n sopimuskausi.,

title: Capital Experience Events Catering
description: Reissue of Request for Standing Offers. This request for standing offers (RFSO) cancels and supersedes previous RFSO number 10251648 dated November 20, 2025 with a closing of January 15, 2026 at 14:00 EST. The mandate of Canadian Heritage’s (PCH) Capital Celebrations and Program Operations directorate is to organize major events in the National Capital Region (NCR). In the context of some of these events, catering services will be required for artists, programming partners, volunteers, technical crew and staff at selected locations in the NCR. The purpose of this Request for Standing Offer (RFSO) is to establish up to two (2) Standing Offers from date of award to December 31, 2028 with the possibility of extending by up to one (1) additional one-year option period, with qualified Offerors who can provide catering services on an “as and when” requested basis during PCH’s major events and other events. M1 Bidder’s Experience The Bidder must demonstrate their experience providing catering services for large-scale, high-profile events within the last five (5) years as of the closing date of this solicitation, by providing detailed descriptions for three (3) separate catering events. A” large-scale, high-profile” event would be one that: • Had 200 or more guests present simultaneously; and, • Included as attendees at least two (2) high-profile guests like public figures and/or performing artists. NB: • At least one of the events must have been for buffet style service. • At least one of the events must have been for boxed meal style service. Each event description must include: • A description of the event for which the catering was done (name, nature of the event); • The physical location of the event • The number of guests that attended simultaneously; • A description of the high-profile guests that were in attendance (without identifying by name); • The format of the food service (boxed meals, plated, buffet, etc.); and, • Any other pertinent information that describes the nature of the project. MT2 Proposed Menus The Bidder must propose two (2) sample menus. Each of the menus must correspond to the minimum requirements for the following meal and format types as described in the section 3.4 Estimated Meal Requirements: 1. Continental Breakfast Buffet 2. Dinner Buffet; 3. Boxed Lunch; and, 4. Boxed Dinner. MT3 Food Allergies and Intolerances and special instructions The Bidder must describe their protocol when managing boxed meal service when there are special instructions concerning food intolerances and allergies. The protocol must include: • How the special instructions are transmitted to the kitchen; • What measures the kitchen takes to respect the special instructions; • How meal boxes are prepared when there are special instructions; • If there are particular protocols when preparing meal boxes that have particular instructions (e.g. nut allergies); • How the meal boxes are identified before delivery; and, • Any other relevant information

title: Gather data and maintain the alternative fuel station database
description: Within NRCan, the Transportation and Fuels Decarbonization Programs Branch (TFDPB) promotes energy conservation and use of low carbon fuels is committed to undertaking initiatives designed to reduce fuel use and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Canada in support of Canada’s climate goals TFDP, in coordination with the United States Department of Energy’s National Laboratories of the Rockies (NLR), aims to continue adding and updating Canadian Electric Charging and Alternative refuelling infrastructure locations to NLR’s web based Alternative Fuels Station Locator. For more than a decade NLR has provided this technical resource, which has taken the form of vehicle and fleet evaluations, data development and analysis, development of on-line tools and resources, and overall integration and management of this base of knowledge in Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC) managed by NLR. (http://www.afdc.energy.gov/locator/stations/) TFDPB’s Infrastructure Programs manages this and the related contracts.

title: EÜ-Dahlweg, Brücke und Gleise
description: CargoBeamer ist ein international tätiger Logistikdienstleister mit Sitz in Deutschland und bietet im kombinierten Verkehr innovative Lösungen, um kranbare und nicht kranbare Sattelauflieger umweltfreundlich über die Schiene zu transportieren. Die CargoBeamer Terminal Kaldenkirchen GmbH beabsichtigt den Ersatzneubau der Eisenbahnüberführung EÜ Dahlweg in Nettetal-Kaldenkirchen im Bereich des CargoBeamer-Terminals. Das bestehende Bauwerk befindet sich bei Bahn-km 18,490 der Strecke 2510 Viersen–Kaldenkirchen im Bereich des Ausziehgleises 21 und überführt die Gleisanlage über den Dahlweg. Bei dem Bestandsbauwerk handelt es sich um eine Gewölbebrücke aus Ziegelmauerwerk mit Schrägflügeln. Aufgrund des baulichen Zustands und des Alters ist ein vollständiger Ersatzneubau vorgesehen. Die Vergabe erfolgt als funktionale Generalübernehmerleistung mit Pauschalvergütung. Der Auftragnehmer übernimmt die gemäß den Vergabeunterlagen geschuldeten Planungs-, Genehmigungs-, Untersuchungs-, Koordinierungs-, Rückbau- und Bauleistungen einschließlich der erforderlichen Prüfungen, Dokumentation und Übergabe eines vollständig funktionsfähigen und abnahmefähigen Bauwerks.

title: Ireland – Panel vans – Supply of a Road Transport Vehicle (Commercial Van) as part of the PEACEPLUS Mini Digi Hubs Project
description: The supply, delivery, registration and commissioning of one new commercial panel van together with all mandatory equipment, conversion works and associated documentation . The van will operate as a Mobile Digital Van (“MDV”) in support of the PEACEPLUS Mini Digi Hubs Project, a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). The MDV will provide a flexible, dual-purpose operational capability by: (a) supporting rapid “light deployments” through the transportation of up to three persons, digital learning equipment, ICT resources and project materials to schools, community centres and other suitable host venues, where project activities may be delivered indoors using the host venue’s available broadband connectivity; and (b) serving as the towing and logistics vehicle for the PEACEPLUS Mobile Digital Lab (“MDL”), with the capability to safely and reliably tow the MDL, which has a maximum trailer mass of 3,500 kg. The Goods include all vehicle equipment, towing equipment, conversion works, security systems, vehicle graphics, registration, delivery, commissioning, documentation, warranty and associated support services specified in the RFT.

title: NX EQ Microscope Spine
description: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Microscope: Spine product line as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as �national�) single Requirements contract award. The microscope provides a stable, maneuverable platform with motorized zoom and focus, long working?distance lenses, and high?intensity illumination suitable for deep spinal corridors. It supports hybrid optical/digital viewing, allowing the surgeon to operate through traditional eyepieces or external large?format 3D monitors. Integrated imaging capabilities provide 4K or higher?resolution video and still capture for clinical documentation, teaching, and intraoperative collaboration. title: International Recovery - Mexico (Follow-On)
description: Synopsis � 83310127Q0012 | Claim(s) in Mexico (Follow-on) EXIM Bank, headquartered in Washington, D.C., is providing this notice of intent to issue a sole source a follow-on award to provide asset protection and recovery services. The applicable Product/Service Code is R418. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541110 - Offices of Lawyers, which has a size standard of $16M. This requirement is to assist EXIM in its efforts to collect outstanding amounts owed to EXIM by the obligor/buyer and all guarantors, if any. These efforts will include, as EXIM may direct, asset searches, site visits, negotiations, litigation, documentation of agreements, embargoing assets and executing upon assets. See attached PWS. When an individual AMD recovery contract ends but the recovery action is still pending resolution, we award follow-on contracts on a sole source basis to the original vendor (per FAR 16.505(2)(c)) as long as it is for the same recovery case(s). The rationale for this is the combination of contingency payment agreement and the frequent long length of the recovery process. With limited vendor availability, if we did not follow this practice, the original vendor could perform most of the work and the subsequent vendor would reap the rewards of any funds recovered. By awarding follow-on contracts in this manner, we establish fairness for the vendors in an unusual situation, retain good relations with a limited vendor pool for future needs, and therefore get the best long-term benefit to the government. Place of Contract Performance: EXIM Bank in Washington, D.C. and Mexico Contracting Point of Contact and/or Contracting Officer: Travis Finkle Travis.Finkle@exim.gov Contracting Office Address: Office of Contract Services 811 Vermont Ave., NW Washington, DC 20571

description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von Kamera und Ventil Baugruppen des Systems GTK Boxer. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet am 31.12.2030. Des Weiteren behält sich der Auftraggeber eine optionale Verlängerung der Rahmenvereinbarung bis zum 31.12.2033 vor. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

title: France – Non-hazardous refuse and waste treatment and disposal services – Marché global de performance (MGP) pour la modernisation et l'exploitation de l'unité de traitement et de valorisation énergétique de Rillieux-la-Pape (UTVE Lyon nord)
description: La consultation a pour objet la contractualisation d'un Marché Global de Performance au sens de l'article L. 2171-3 du Code de la Commande Publique. Le Marché portera sur la conception et la réalisation des travaux visés dans le programme fonctionnel et exigentiel et l'exploitation de l'usine de valorisation énergétique des déchets de la Métropole de Lyon à Rillieux-la-Pape. Les principales prestations à la charge du Titulaire sont les suivantes : - Conception et réalisation de travaux de modernisation visant à améliorer les performances de l'UTVE, - Démarches administratives pour le changement de titulaire des arrêtés, et pour l'obtention des autorisations préalables à la réalisation des travaux, Exploitation, entretien courant et gros entretien renouvellement (GER) de l'UTVE dans le respect de la continuité de service, de la réglementation en vigueur et en conformité avec les objectifs de la Métropole de Lyon, - Fourniture de chaleur au réseau de Rillieux-la-Pape, - Commercialisation de l'électricité après autoconsommation de l'UTVE, - Commercialisation des sous-produits (à minima des ferreux et non-ferreux) de l'UTVE, - Gestion des résidus d'incinération (évacuation et valorisation ou stockage). Le besoin mis en concurrence fait l'objet d'un lot unique. 1 Tranche ferme : Conception et réalisation de travaux de modernisation de l'UTVE ; l'exploitation et la maintenance de l'UTVE. 1 Tranche optionnelle : Conception et réalisation de travaux permettant le traitement de boues de STEP par l'UTVE ; l'exploitation et la maintenance de l'UTVE avec le dispositif de traitement des boues de STEP

title: INDUSTRY DAY: FORT HUNTER LIGGETT BARRACKS PDB-OTA
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for the design and construction of four (4) Collective Training Enlisted (CTE) Barracks and one (1) Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks at Fort Hunter Liggett, CA using Progressive Design-Build (PDB) under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 17 November 2026 at 0900 Pacific Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed Progressive Design-Build (PDB) approach under an Other Transaction (OT) framework, ask questions, and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions from industry participants will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute a commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future Request for Qualifications (RFQ). Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. To access Fort Hunter Liggett, please proceed directly to the Main Gate / Access Control Point. You must be a U.S. Citizen and have a REAL ID to complete registration. If you do not have a REAL ID, provide your valid State ID/Driver�s License plus a current U.S. Passport. Please state your business intention �attending the U.S. Army Corps of Engineer�s Industry Day at Bldg. 3300�. Individuals with a valid CAC, should be able to access the installation directly. Fort Hunter Liggett Access Control Point Address: 2Q26+W3C Fort Hunter Liggett, CA 93928; or 36�00'08.3"N 121�14'23.5"W II. LOCATION/LOGISTICS Industry Day Presentation location: Building 3300, Classrooms 118 & 119. Parking is at the rear of the building. Overflow parking is located at Longbow St. and Blackhawk St. Fort Hunter Liggett Building 3300 Address: XQX8+V2, Fort Hunter Liggett, CA 93928; or 36�00'00.0"N 121�14'05.9"W USACE Agency Representative Mr. Robert �Bob� Roy � USACE Project Engineer, Sacramento District (831)710-7154 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Design and Construction of four (4) Collective Training Enlisted (CTE) Barracks and one (1) Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks Location: Fort Hunter Liggett, California Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This acquisition will deliver four (4) Collective Training Enlisted (CTE) Barracks and one (1) Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks at Fort Hunter Liggett, CA. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to demolish and dispose of five (5) existing Barracks and replacing with four (4) CTE Barracks and one (1) AST Barracks. Key features of the project may include: Design and construct four (4) multi-story CTE Barracks (approximately 46,000 total SF each), which will feature open bays, along with integrated officers sleeping rooms, team rooms, laundry facilities, restrooms, showers, storage, and janitorial closets. Supporting facilities may include but not limited to; site development, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, walks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, HVAC, information systems, landscaping, signage, sustainability/energy, cybersecurity, and all required fixtures, furnishings, and equipment. Design and construct one (1) multi-story AST Barracks (approximately 45,000 total SF), which will feature sleeping quarters with bathrooms, study/day rooms, laundry rooms, storage, and janitorial closets. Supporting facilities may include but not limited to; site development, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, walks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, HVAC, information systems, landscaping, signage, sustainability/energy, cybersecurity, and all required fixtures, furnishings, and equipment. Demolish and dispose of five (5) existing multi-story Barracks (approximately 39,000 total SF each). V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE, Louisville District will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � White Papers: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (max # of pages to be defined in formal RFQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to down-select up to three (3) highest qualified firms to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Down-selected firms will participate in live pitch meetings. One company will be selected to enter exclusive negotiations. The Agreements Officer will request a detailed price proposal for Phase 1 (100% design) and negotiate the design fee, payment milestones, and Agreement Articles. The Government intends to negotiate a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for construction, which will be added as a bilateral modification at a later date. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified Design/Builder to provide design, preconstruction services, and construction. Phase 1 of the Progressive Design Build agreement will include design development and pre-construction services. Phase 2 of the agreement will include scope for all construction activities necessary to complete the project. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal Project RFQ. VII. Virtual Participation Opportunity: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day even in person, the Louisville District plans to stream the event through Microsoft Teams. title: FY27 HIOSH Hazardous Waste
description: The purpose of this amendment 01 is to provide a revise RFQ with a revised SOW. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) operates basic science research facilities in Cincinnati, Ohio; Morgantown, West Virginia; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; and Spokane, Washington. Each location generates hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste through research and laboratory operations. Each location is considered a Small Quantity Generator of hazardous waste. The approximate average monthly quantities generated are: Location Approximate Monthly Quantity Cincinnati, Ohio 100 pounds Morgantown, West Virginia 500 pounds Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 150 pounds Spokane, Washington 50 pounds Each location shall be treated as a separate job site. Hazardous waste shall be collected quarterly from designated collection areas. Contractor personnel shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. The acquisition is being pursued to obtain compliant collection, packaging, transportation, documentation, treatment, and final disposal services for waste generated at NIOSH facilities. The contractor shall provide complete cradle-to-final-disposal services and maintain the documentation necessary to demonstrate proper management of each waste stream. Performance shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including, as applicable, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Toxic Substances Control Act, the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Hazardous Materials Transportation Act, applicable United States Department of Transportation regulations in 49 CFR Parts 100�199, and applicable requirements in 40 CFR Parts 261 and 264/265. PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain safe, lawful, and fully documented management of hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste generated at four NIOSH research facilities. The contractor shall provide all personnel, labor, supervision, transportation, packaging, equipment, supplies, supplies, permits, licenses, analysis, documentation, and other resources necessary to: Collect waste from designated collection areas; Package and label waste for shipment; Prepare and process required manifests and shipping documents; Transport waste in compliance with applicable requirements; Determine appropriate treatment or disposal methods; Ensure waste is delivered to properly permitted facilities; Complete final treatment or final disposal; and Provide documentation and audit trails demonstrating the ultimate disposition of each waste item. The contractor shall perform all work in a safe, prudent, conscientious, and professional manner. Work shall be performed during NIOSH normal working hours and shall comply with all applicable safety, environmental, transportation, and security requirements. SCOPE OF WORK The contractor shall provide quarterly removal of listed waste streams for the Cincinnati, Morgantown, Pittsburgh, and Spokane NIOSH locations. Each site shall be considered a separate job for scheduling, pickup, invoicing, documentation, and performance purposes. The contractor shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. All hazardous chemicals waste, universal waste, additional waste listed below, and gas cylinders are not associated with all four sites. Waste may include the following: Hazardous chemical waste Flammable liquids, including alcohol, xylene, acetonitrile, and ethyl acetate; Non-pouring flammables, including gas cylinders, solids, and metal powders; Inorganic and organic acids; Inorganic and organic bases; Oxidizers; Solid metals and metal powders; U-listed and P-listed wastes; Peroxides and reactive waste; Mercury compounds; Non-RCRA solids and liquids; Dioxin; Pentachlorophenol and polychlorinated biphenyl waste; Flammable aerosols; Formaldehyde, formaldehyde solutions, and glutaraldehyde-containing tissue specimens; Small quantities of explosives, generally from 1 to 1,000 grams; Paints; Sodium cacodylate; Potassium cacodylate; Waste oil; and Used or expired self-contained self-rescuer cartridges. Universal waste Batteries; Pesticides; Mercury-containing equipment; Lamps; and Aerosol cans. Additional waste Used oils; Charcoal filters; and Aqueous waste. Gas cylinders Toxic, corrosive, flammable, oxidizing, or refrigerant gas cylinders; Majority of cylinders are high pressure steel, 9-10�D X 48-51�H Some cylinders in Pittsburgh have unidentified contents. Gas-cylinder removal shall be provided as a separate line item. The estimated quantities are: Location Estimated Cylinders Cincinnati, Ohio 0 Morgantown, West Virginia 10 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 75 Spokane, Washington 15 Gas cylinders may be removed in one service event or over the life of the contract. Once removed, the cylinders are not expected to be replaced. The contractor shall provide lab-packs, drums, overpacks, packaging materials, labels, and other equipment necessary to safely consolidate, package, transport, and dispose of the waste. The contractor shall remain responsible for proper management of waste after it leaves NIOSH property, including transportation, spills, leaks, treatment, final disposal, and supporting documentation. TASKS TO BE PERFORMED Task 1: Provide Waste Collection and Packaging Services The contractor shall schedule and perform quarterly waste pickups at each NIOSH location. a. The contractor shall coordinate pickup dates with the designated NIOSH representative. b. The contractor shall collect waste from designated collection areas. c. The contractor shall not require access to individual laboratories. d. The contractor shall treat each NIOSH location as a separate job for scheduling and invoicing. The contractor shall provide all packaging and handling services required for safe shipment. a. The contractor shall supply lab-packs, drums, overpacks, labels, containers, absorbent materials, and other necessary packaging. b. The contractor shall package waste in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor shall not require separation of tissue from formaldehyde solutions containing tissue. d. The contractor shall identify and manage incompatible waste streams appropriately. The contractor shall provide a separate line item for gas-cylinder removal. a. The contractor shall remove gas cylinders identified by NIOSH. b. The contractor shall manage cylinders with known or unidentified contents in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor may remove cylinders during one service event or over the life of the contract. Task 2: Provide Transportation, Treatment, and Final Disposal Services The contractor shall transport waste in accordance with all applicable requirements. a. The contractor shall comply with United States Department of Transportation requirements in 49 CFR Parts 100�199. b. The contractor shall ensure that all approved subcontractors and transporters comply with applicable transportation requirements. c. The contractor shall ensure that shipping papers include required technical names, emergency-response information, and a 24-hour emergency telephone number. d. The contractor shall ensure that off-site shipments are properly labeled, marked, and placarded. The contractor shall provide final treatment and final disposal of all waste. a. The contractor shall send waste only to licensed, permitted, and approved facilities. b. The contractor shall ensure that each facility is authorized to handle the applicable waste streams and RCRA waste codes. c. Mere acceptance of waste at a treatment, storage, or disposal facility shall not constitute final treatment or final disposal. d. The contractor shall obtain documentation demonstrating completion of final treatment or final disposal. The contractor shall provide all required personnel, labor, equipment, permits, licenses, transportation, supplies, and services at no additional cost to the Government unless expressly authorized by the contract. title: Z1DA--Design Build | NRM 654-27-130 | Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide VASNHCS
description: SOURCES SOUGHT DESIGN BUILD 36C26127R0011 This is a pre-solicitation notice under FAR 5.203(a), FAR 5.204, and FAR 36.601-1, and FAR 36.3 of the Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21 intent to contract for a Design Build Contract for the VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System (VASNHCS) Project No. 654-27-130, Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide, located at VASNHCS, Reno, Nevada. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, and the small business size standard is $45 Million. A construction firm shall be responsible for both the design and construction of the project. This design effort includes, but is not limited to, providing Schematic Design (SDs), Design Development (DDs), Construction Documents (CDs), and Construction Period Services (CPS) necessary to perform construction to Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide at VASNHCS. The contract work requires multiple disciplines for the design. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm. The disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Structural, Plumbing, Fire Life Safety, Sustainability, Security, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Way-Finding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Interested parties are advised that in keeping with the Veterans First Contracting program under 38 U.S.C. 8127-8128, as implemented under VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) subpart 819.70 and VA Procurement Policy Memorandum 2016-05 Implementation of the Veterans First Contracting Program, if the Contracting Officer has a reasonable expectation that two or more small business concerns owned and controlled by Service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns will submit responses to the solicitation and that award can be made at a fair and reasonable price that offers the best value to the United States, the requirement will be set-aside for SDVOSB concerns. If an SDVOSB set-aside is not appropriate, the requirement will be evaluated to determine whether a Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) set-aside is appropriate. The term SDVOSB / VOSB under the Veterans First Contracting program has the same meaning as defined in FAR subpart 2.101, except for acquisitions authorized by 38 U.S.C. 8127 and 8128 for the Veterans First Contracting Program SDVOSB and VOSB concerns must be listed as verified in the SBA Small Business Search (SBS) database at https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ in addition to meeting the NAICS code small business size standard to be eligible for award under Veterans First Contracting Program set-asides. Interested parties are encouraged to provide the following capability information to the Contract Specialist, Nicole Renfrew, via email at Nicole.Renfrew@va.gov by 10:00 A.M. Pacific Standard Time on November 17, 2026. Please complete the attached form with the following information: Business Size (Large/Small) Business Socio-Economic Status (SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.) Copy of current SAM record SAM Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number Copy of SBA SBS record showing verified status: SDVOSB/VOSB concerns only. Bonding Capacity: Provide your surety name, your maximum bonding capacity per project and your aggregate maximum bonding capacity. The bonding capacity per project must be $5 Million to be deemed acceptable for this notice. The Government will use this information when determining its business set-aside decision, taking into consideration the requirements outlined in VA Procurement Policy Memorandum 2016-05 Implementation of the Veterans First Contracting Program. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be issued on or about December 01, 2026. It is the intent of the Government to make a single firm-fixed price Design Build contract award for this requirement. Questions regarding this Sources Sought notice should be directed, in writing, to the Contract Specialist Nicole Renfrew, via email at Nicole.Renfrew@va.gov. This synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government and no contract will be awarded as a direct result of this Sources Sought announcement. description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. Transitioning to a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model is critical to eliminate traditional design-bid-build delays, rapidly deliver compliant spaces, and preserve the security mission of the 30th Space Wing. There are (2) two distinct lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) IDIQ Contract
description: The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Systems Command (SSC), intends to award a sole-source Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to The Boeing Company (CAGE: 18600), P.O. Box 92919, Los Angeles, CA 90009-2919, for the Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) effort. The anticipated contract will have a five-year base ordering period and one ten-year optional ordering period, with a total estimated ceiling of approximately $945.9M ($480.6M base and $465.3M option) if all options are exercised. This IDIQ contract will provide the critical, full life-cycle engineering, sustainment, cybersecurity, modernization, and operational enhancement support for multiple Military Satellite Communications (MILSATCOM) constellations. The scope of this requirement includes, but is not limited to: Space Vehicle & Constellation Sustainment: 24/7 real-time anomaly analysis, fault isolation, and recovery; factory reachback engineering; telemetry trending; orbital analysis; maneuver planning; collision avoidance (COLA); and end-of-life (EOL) disposal for the Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and Ultra High Frequency Follow-On (UFO) satellite constellations. Ground Command & Control Support: Sustaining engineering, software maintenance, and enhancement for the Global SATCOM Configuration and Control Element (GSCCE) ground system. Software, Database, & Simulation Sustainment: Maintenance and updates for satellite flight software, the Satellite Simulator (SATSIM), operational databases, and engineering tools. Pre-Handover & Transition Support: Support for the transition of new space vehicles (e.g., WGS-11, WGS-12) and hosted payloads (e.g., Protected Tactical SATCOM Prototype [PTS-P]) from development into the operational sustainment baseline. Statutory Authority: This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Justification for Sole Source: The Boeing Company is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the WGS satellites, UFO satellites, and critical components of the GSCCE ground system. Boeing possesses unique qualifications and exclusive ownership of the proprietary data, software, and specialized infrastructure required to perform this sustainment effort. The Government does not possess sufficient data license rights for the technical data packages (TDPs), flight software source code, or high-fidelity satellite simulators (SATSIM) to permit a competitive acquisition. This proprietary data, which was developed at private expense, includes detailed design documentation for the Boeing 702HP and 702MP satellite platforms, simulators, and ground control software. Boeing has repeatedly declined the Government�s requests to sell the necessary data rights. Without access to this OEM-owned data, no other contractor can perform the required engineering and sustainment without introducing substantial duplication of cost to the Government and unacceptable delays and risk to on-orbit assets critical to national security. Market research confirmed that Boeing is the only contractor fully capable of satisfying all of the requirements of this acquisition without a break in critical service to the warfighter.

title: Cleaning C and D Towers Phoenix Main Hospital
description: The Contractor shall provide complete, coordinated, and documented cleaning and mold-prevention services for seven 8th-floor plenum chambers and associated air-handling components serving inpatient areas. The work shall prevent cross-contamination into patient-care spaces, support acceptable indoor air quality, and leave treated areas ready for VA inspection and acceptance. The 8th-floor plenum chambers and associated air-handling components in the C and D Towers support inpatient areas. Mold contamination has been identified in the past. This preventive project covers seven chambers, adjacent ductwork, and concrete surfaces and is required to maintain air quality and prevent cross-contamination into patient-care spaces.

title: GA-VGMS-33528
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology & Calibration (AFMETCAL) program office is seeking sources capable of providing an upgrade to a primary vacuum standard. Work includes integrating additional hardware to the system, updating the proprietary software, and verifying performance of upgrade onsite to allow calibration of analog output vacuum gauges. Work includes correction of various issues with software bugs. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity of 1 unit over 1 year. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27M-638A-VA in all correspondence. Responses are due by 11/17/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if issued. The purpose of this SSN is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors, including large business sources, small business sources and their size classifications (i.e., HUBZone 8(a), 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business, and Small Disadvantaged Business) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. Responses to this SSN will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA/CDRH Scientific Technical Capacity for Regulatory Review Background: To assist the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) in fulfilling its mission, CDRH seeks expert consultants to assist CDRH�s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle. CDRH requires consultants that have skilled experience to assist with medical device regulatory review work and supporting scientific activities, such as research, cybersecurity and digital health consultations, regulatory consultations and auditing, and interacting with industry and patients. The CDRH requires consultants that have sufficient skilled capacity in many science, engineering, and clinical specialties, including Anesthesiology, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Clinical laboratory testing, Computer Science and Engineering, Consumer Safety, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Dentistry, Digital Health, Epidemiology, Gastroenterology, General Engineering, Health Science, Infectious Diseases, Interdisciplinary Engineer/Scientist, Molecular testing, Neurology, Optics, Patient Engagement, Physics, Psychiatry, Public Health, Pulmonology, Reprocessing medical devices, Social Scientist, Software Engineering, Statistics and Biostatistics, Sterilization, Toxicology, Urology, Veterinary Medicine, and Virology. Objective: The primary objective of this effort is to provide the CDRH with a vehicle to acquire the support services of advanced professional and scientific consultants to assist CDRH�s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle, including the supporting scientific, engineering, clinical, and regulatory activities. The services provided will be critical scientific expertise and capacity in support for the evaluation of the continued performance, safety, and effectiveness, with respect to devices approved, cleared, licensed, or authorized for use for the treatment, prevention, or diagnosis of medical conditions by the FDA. Instructions for Responses to this SSN: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). The anticipated period of performance consists of one (1) Base Year and four (4) Option Years. Responses to this SSN must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Does your firm qualify as a Small Disadvantaged Business? If disadvantaged, specify if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Are you considered a certified HUBZone firm? Are you considered Woman-Owned or operated business? Are you a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned or Veteran-Owned business? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (�Attachment A-Draft Statement of Work�). All interested parties can provide written opinions/questions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions/questions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Responses to this SSN shall be submitted via e-mail to Melinda Kim, Contract Specialist, at Melinda.Kim@fda.hhs.gov, (with a CC: to Nicholas Bisher, Contracting Officer, at Nicholas.Bisher@fda.hhs.gov), by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on November 17, 2026. The subject line of the e-mail shall reference, �Vendor Response to SSN 75F40127Q00006.� After a review of the received responses, a formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov or on GSA eBuy. description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Acadia National Park, Project ME NP ACAD BRG(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000002, located in Hancock County, Maine. The project consists of repair of Main Route 233, Paradise Hill, and Frazer Creek Bridges. The work includes reconstruction of asphalt concrete pavement and aggregate base course, placement of structural backfill, cleaning and removing debris from weepholes and inlets, cleaning and sealing joints, erosion repair, repointing mortar joints, placing waterproofing membrane to improve the service life, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 9, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders

title: Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) Request for Information
description: Description NASA�s Commercial Access to Space Program and Launch Services Program Office (LSP) are seeking statements of interest from industry demonstrating the interest, experience, and capability to provide launch services in support of the Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) requirements identified below. General Project Requirements NASA intends to procure launch services through a full and open competition for at least eight (8) full-mission-assurance launches to the following orbits: Two (2) High C3 Orbit in 2031 Two (2) Lagrange/Lunar Orbit in 2030 Three (3) Sun Synchronous Orbit (SSO) in 2030 (2 mission) and 2031 (1 mission) One (1) Low Earth Orbit (LEO) in 2030 These missions will require full NASA insight and full mission assurance; however, they will not require a completed first flight prior to proposal receipt. Full mission assurance is described as a Contractor providing NASA an adequate level of insight into and/or approval of certain Contractor tasks and milestones in order to ensure all reasonable steps have been taken that result in the highest probability of mission success. These requirements are subject to change. Request for Information Goals and Objectives The goal of this RFI is to improve both NASA's understanding of industry capabilities and the industry's understanding of NASA's needs by collecting industry feedback on the planned procurement process and evaluation strategy for the MCLS acquisition. This information will help LSP understand how to best structure the upcoming solicitation and evaluation criteria to align with industry�s best practices and maximize competition. Please complete the attached questionnaire detailing your perspectives on the most effective procurement approach. Industry Day: NASA LSP intends to host a virtual forum with industry (i.e., �Industry Day�) on the 12th and 13th of November 2026 to engage in open discussion and dialogue to answer questions interested parties may have regarding the NASA�s contemplated MCLS acquisition strategy. The objective of this event is to receive industry�s feedback on the MCLS acquisition strategy and provide industry with additional details about the MCLS acquisition. Additionally, if there are any procurement topics you recommend LSP specifically address at Industry Day, please let us know by 10 November 2026. Finally, please indicate if you would like to discuss any topic(s) individually. Immediately following Industry Day, LSP will offer sixty (60)-minute timeslots for one-on-one meetings with each interested party. Timing of these one-on-one meetings is tentative and will depend on the number of RSVPs received, timing of the Industry Day, etc. Those who wish to attend are encouraged to RSVP to the virtual Industry Day and one-on-one meetings as soon as possible, but no later than 9 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. The purpose of this RFI and upcoming Industry Day is to conduct market research for currently available launch capabilities. To be considered within the scope of this effort, the Respondent�s proposed launch vehicle must have development tests demonstrating at least 50% of the flight thrust at the complete full-scale single engine assembly level for all core stage engines of the common launch vehicle configuration being proposed. Launch vehicles that are currently in the conceptual or design stages will not be considered for this specific requirement. Submittal Instructions Please use the Questionnaire document that is provide to answer the RFI questions. All responses should be sent electronically to NASA points of contact identified below NLT 17 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. Any responses submitted through different channels or to a different email may not be considered. When submitting a response, please use the email subject �Response to RFI � NASA MCLS.� Points of Contact Primary Rachel Edwards, Contracting Officer Rachel.t.edwards@nasa.gov Secondary Mary Vaughn, Lead Contracting Officer mary.e.vaughn-1@nasa.gov THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Sources Sought is being issued for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This Sources Sought does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals. Respondents to this notice are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred by responding to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the expense of the responding party. Intellectual or other privileged information contained in responses to this Sources Sought will not be distributed outside of NASA or United States Government employees from other Government agencies.

title: Z2FF-FCI El Reno-Replacement of Housing Unit HVAC Systems
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIDDERS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY.PLEASE DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE IF YOU ARE NOT SERIOUSLY INTERESTED AND IF YOU DO NOT PERFORM THIS REQUIREMENT. IT WILL DELAY THE POSTING OF THE SOLICITATION DUE TO FURTHER MARKET RESEARCH THAT WILL BE REQUIRED. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified contractors to perform a design-build construction project at FCI El Reno, Oklahoma. Responses will be used to assist in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and potential socioeconomic set-aside determination. The Government anticipates issuing a solicitation following completion of market research. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM Central Time (CT) on November 17, 2026. Project Location: FCI El Reno, 4205 Highway 66 West, El Reno, OK 73036 NAICS Code: 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air Conditioning Contractors; Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Project Description The Federal Bureau of Prisons anticipates issuing a Firm-Fixed-Price Design-Build Construction Contract for the replacement and modernization of HVAC systems serving five (5) inmate housing facilities at FCI El Reno. The project consists of providing all design, engineering, labor, supervision, materials, equipment, testing, commissioning, and incidental work required to replace aging direct expansion (DX) cooling systems with a modern chilled-water system serving Housing Units A, B, C, D, and the Special Housing Unit (SHU). Work includes removal and disposal of ten (10) existing DX condensing units and associated equipment; design and installation of ten (10) new air-cooled packaged chillers; installation of ten (10) new chilled-water cooling coils; construction of five (5) chiller equipment pads and five (5) temporary chiller landing pads; installation of chilled-water piping systems; electrical distribution modifications and upgrades; installation of five (5) temporary cooling connection stations and five (5) temporary shore-power connection stations; BAS/DDC controls integration; contractor-provided temporary cooling services during phased construction; and all testing, adjusting, balancing (TAB), commissioning, startup, training, and closeout activities. Work will be performed within an occupied, secure federal correctional institution and will require strict compliance with institutional security requirements. Submission Instructions Interested contractors shall complete the attached questionnaire and submit it via email to Jose Dominguez at jdominguez@bop.gov. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM Central Time (CT) on November 17, 2026. Vendors are also encouraged to add their name to the Interested Vendors List in SAM.gov.
