title: Public Accountant Contract Audits (PACA) Installation Audits (USAFE region)
description: The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders. All interested quoters are invited to submit questions by 2:00PM, CST, Monday, 9 November 2026. Submit all quotes no later than (NLT) 2:00PM, CST, Tuesdsy, 17 Nov 2026 via email to valerie.baltimore@us.af.mil and whitney.ward.1@us.af.mil. The RFQ closes at 2:00PM, CST, Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026.

title: NIH Scientific & Technical Expertise & Acquisition Management (STEAM)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE NIH SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL EXPERTISE ACQUISITION & MANAGEMENT (STEAM) Sources Sought Reference Number: 75N98027R00012 Proposed NAICS Code and Size Standard: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Services; $19.5 million in average annual receipts Sources Sought Notice Information Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) their small business and applicable socioeconomic status, including HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, veteran-owned, 8(a), woman-owned, and small disadvantaged business status; and (3) their size classification relative to the proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a full or partial small business set-aside is appropriate. Interested small businesses may respond for Task Area A (Professional Services), Task Area B (Highly Specialized Scientific Services), or both. Respondents should identify their ability to perform as a prime contractor, joint venture, or subcontracting team, distinguish their own capability from that of team members, and identify limitations within each task area addressed. NIH will assess capability separately for each area. Capability in both areas is not required to respond. The Government has not made a final set-aside determination. Background The National Institutes of Health (NIH) conducts and supports biomedical and behavioral research to advance scientific knowledge and improve health. NIH requires professional, scientific, and technical contractor support for current and emerging research priorities, ongoing research activities, and related program operations. Changes in research programs and scientific methods create a continuing need for flexible service delivery and specialized expertise. Scientific & Technical Expertise Acquisition & Management (STEAM) will acquire contractor-provided services and expertise to accomplish varied project-based requirements across NIH. Individual task orders will define project objectives, tasks, deliverables or milestones, performance periods, required expertise, and resource needs. Contractors must furnish and manage the resources needed to perform multiple concurrent projects at substantial volume and adjust those resources as authorized project requirements change. NIH anticipates using cost-reimbursement contracting approximately 20 percent of the time. The actual mix will depend on individual requirements. Firms should describe their experience and ability to support this component, including any preparation needed. Existing cost-reimbursement capability or a prior Government accounting-system approval is not a mandatory condition of responding to this notice. Applicable requirements, including accounting-system adequacy, would need to be satisfied before award of a cost-reimbursement order. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of STEAM is to provide professional, scientific, and technical support for NIH research and related activities. Support includes basic, translational, and clinical research; vaccine research; general and specialized laboratory research; veterinary and animal research support; bioinformatics; computational biology; and related professional and technical services. The contractor will furnish and manage qualified resources to accomplish each statement of work (SOW), including responsibility for recruiting, verifying qualifications, retaining its personnel, and maintaining continuity of performance. Services will be furnished under individual funded, project-based task orders. The contractor will furnish resources, including personnel with expertise corresponding to the applicable labor categories, to accomplish the SOW and deliver the required project outcomes and milestones. The contractor will retain responsibility for employing, supervising, and managing its personnel. Services will not include inherently governmental functions or unauthorized personal services. Each task order will identify the applicable task area, project scope, qualifications, location, performance schedule, and security and safety requirements. Project Requirements Services may involve expertise in microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, infectious diseases, immunology, clinical research, bioinformatics, genomic sequencing, proteomics, image analysis, computational and systems biology, and scientific data analysis. Related requirements may include clinical trials support, laboratory operations, veterinary services, program management, and other professional or technical support within the authorized scope. Qualifications range from positions without a degree requirement to licensed practitioners and highly specialized doctoral-level professionals. The contractor must be able to furnish qualified resources within the task area or areas addressed and manage a substantial volume of concurrent project requirements. Primary anticipated locations include Bethesda and Rockville, Maryland; other locations in the Washington, DC metropolitan area; and Hamilton, Montana. Other domestic locations, overseas support, travel, or remote work may be authorized by individual orders. NIH-wide demand for task orders and contractor support fluctuates across projects, locations, and time. This notice does not provide a fixed annual volume estimate or guarantee a minimum workload. Routine task orders will establish mobilization, onboarding, and performance start schedules. Under certain circumstances, an urgent or unforeseen NIH need may require the contractor to begin authorized performance within 48 hours. For an expedited request, NIH will identify the applicable timeframe and the event from which it is measured. Respondents should describe their ability to accommodate these requests, identify the categories and locations they could support, and explain any limitations or prerequisites. Contractors must ensure that their personnel have the qualifications and relevant experience required for the assigned work and complete applicable training, competency verification, occupational health requirements, and facility-specific access approvals before beginning restricted work. For assignments involving regulated select agents or toxins, applicable individual access approvals, security risk assessments, and required training must be completed before access. Prior experience at another laboratory does not establish authorization at the receiving NIH facility. An expedited task-order request does not waive these prerequisites. The following 156 labor-category families are organized into two task areas. Each family appears once. Categories encompass applicable levels and specialties; task orders will specify required duties and qualifications. Numbered levels are not automatically equivalent to Junior, Mid-Level, or Senior designations. The task-area structure supports market research and does not establish the final award structure. Task Area A � Professional Services This area covers general professional, management, administrative, business, IT, and technical support for NIH projects, including project coordination, financial analysis, enterprise systems, and related operational services. Scientific versions of otherwise general roles are assigned to Task Area B. title: Z1DA--NRM-CON-663A4-27-001 Under Dispenser Containment (UDC) and sump installation at VAMC American Lake
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for construction services. Solicitation 36C26027R0029 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). This solicitation is conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation, and FAR Part 36, Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts, as applicable, including any Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) deviations in effect on the solicitation issue date. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested. This solicitation is a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. The associated NAICS code is 237120, Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction, and the small business size standard is $45.0 million in average annual receipts. To be eligible for consideration and award, an offeror must meet all of the following at the time of proposal submission and at the time of award: 1. Be certified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), with active certification shown in the SBA database. 2. Have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), www.sam.gov, that lists NAICS code 237120 and represents the offeror as a small business under that NAICS code. 3. Offerors must submit a bid bond with their proposal. An offeror that does not meet these requirements will be ineligible for award. DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Puget Sound Health Care System, has a requirement for a Contractor to provide Under Dispenser Containment (UDC) and Sump Installation, Project 663A4-27-001, at the American Lake Campus, 9600 Veterans Drive SW, Tacoma, WA 98493. SITE VISIT: One site visit is scheduled for November 10, 2026, from 08:00 to 11:00 a.m. PST at the American Lake Campus. Advance confirmation of attendance is required. See Attachment: Site Visit, for instructions. TERMS: This requirement incorporates one or more clauses and provisions by reference, with the same force and effect as if they were given in full text. The full text of a clause or provision may be accessed at http://www.acquisition.gov/far/index.html and http://www.va.gov/oal/library/vaar/. Offerors are encouraged to, and responsible for, reviewing the full solicitation (attached) for the detailed requirement description, applicable terms and conditions, provisions, proposal submission instructions, and evaluation procedures before submitting proposals. All offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), www.sam.gov, at the time of submittal. QUESTIONS: Any questions about this requirement must be sent by email only to derek.crockett@va.gov no later than 12:00 PST on November 12, 2026. Solicitation 36C26027R0029 in the subject line of the email. Responses to questions will be posted as an amendment to the solicitation once the question period has expired. Offerors are responsible for monitoring Contracting Opportunities at www.sam.gov for any amendments, as the Government will not send notice of amendments. Representatives of potential offerors shall not contact any VA Medical Center representative to discuss or inquire about this solicitation. Telephonic questions will not be accepted.

title: Golf Course Driving Range at Ramstein Air Base, Germany
description: This requirement will be solicited among local European sources that can meet the customer's needs listed below. Statement of Needs for Golf Course Driving Range/Woodlawn Driving Range: 1.0 Requirement: Install golf ball tracking technology at the driving range all (18 bays) to provide customers with real time data for practicing/playing purposes. Contractor will install the minimum required cameras/radars to capture data for the entire driving range operating at full capacity. Contractor will install monitors at each bay (18) in an area that is easily viewable by customers but out of the way and protected by the weather. Contactor will install wire tracks as needed, reducing the number of exposed wires. Contractor will return the facility to the same condition as it was before installation began. Contractor will be able to provide a virtual rendering of Woodlawn Golf Course for virtual playing. 1.1 Golf course provides the following: Install power and internet drops in each bay (18). Trenching for power/data cables. Access to the work location during the hours of operation: Monday � Friday, 0600 � 1800 hours. Weekend hours to be discussed as needed.

description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Lakehurst, NJ, intends to issue a sole-source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) with Textron Systems Corporation (CAGE: 97384). This BOA will provide for the procurement of assessment, evaluation, inspection, and repair services for the Multi-Spectral Test Set (MSTS), Part Numbers (P/N) EU04618-01-FG and EU04618-02-FG, in support of the CV-22 aircraft variant. This BOA will be established under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 811219 (Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance) and Product Service Code (PSC) J066 (Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Instruments and Laboratory Equipment). Textron Systems Corporation is the sole designer, developer, integrator, and the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the MSTS. This contracting action is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, 'Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.' All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which will be considered by the agency. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Subcontracting opportunities should be sought directly from Textron Systems Corporation.
